question: Does B-cosification really turn pretrained CNNs, vision transformers, and CLIP into inherently interpretable models while retaining their useful behavior at lower cost, and do its algebra, localization proxies, statistics, artifact, and current competitors support the breadth of that claim?

key_findings.claim: The central technical contribution is a conditional conversion recipe that makes a conventional network a B-cos model at B=1 before changing its behavior through fine-tuning.
key_findings.evidence: A B-cos layer computes |cos(x,w)|^(B-1) times the normalized-weight projection, so at B=1 it reduces to a linear projection. The paper pairs this with a six-channel inverse-color encoding, retained ReLU gates, unnormalized pretrained weights, bias removal, uncentered normalization, and pooling changes. This is a useful architecture-engineering result, but only the B=1 construction is intended to preserve the original function; setting B=2 and deleting biases changes it and requires retraining.

key_findings.claim: The six-channel RGB transformation is an exact and reusable equivalence argument, not merely a heuristic initialization.
key_findings.evidence: The normalized RGB input is mapped to [r,g,b,1-r,1-g,1-b], while the first-layer weights become [w_r/2,w_g/2,w_b/2,-w_r/2,-w_g/2,-w_b/2]. Their inner product recovers the original centered RGB projection. This provides colored positive-versus-negative evidence while preserving the first-layer linear response under the stated preprocessing convention.

anchors.section: Section 3.2.1, image encoding and functionally equivalent initialization

key_findings.claim: The paper's exact W(x)x decomposition establishes algebraic completeness for a specified scalar, but not human interpretability, semantic validity, causal use, or robustness.
key_findings.evidence: Removing biases lets the network be summarized as y(x)=W(x)x, with input-coordinate contributions that reconstruct the output under the model's dynamic gates. Exact reconstruction is a valuable faithfulness contract. It does not by itself show that the displayed pixels are understandable to people, are the causal features the model would use under intervention, are stable under innocuous changes, or correspond to desired rather than spurious evidence; none of those properties follows from the algebra.

key_findings.claim: Increasing B and removing biases produces a sharp localization gain in the ResNet-18 ablation, while showing that the chosen recipe is a simple compromise rather than the empirical optimum.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 reports the standard model at 69.6% accuracy and 21.4 GridPG, B=1 at 70.6/33.9, B=1.5 at 71.6/84.3, B=2 at 71.5/87.6, and learned B at 71.8/89.4. Table 3 reports 71.2/47.2 with biases, 71.5/87.6 without them, and 71.6/91.2 with bias decay 0.9. The authors nevertheless choose immediate B=2 and zero bias for simplicity.

key_findings.claim: Across the headline ImageNet panel, B-cosification improves over training a B-cos model from scratch on average, but does not consistently recover the original pretrained model.
key_findings.evidence: Table 4 reports an average 2.5-point gain over the corresponding scratch B-cos models and an average 5.2x epoch-based speedup. Yet several converted models remain below the starting checkpoint: ResNet-50 v2 falls from 80.9% to 77.3%, ViT-Ti from 70.3% to 69.3%, ViT-L from 75.8% to 75.5%, and ViTc-L from 77.9% to 77.1%. Two large ViTc models show no speedup. The appropriate claim is strong reuse relative to scratch B-cos training, not universal preservation of pretrained performance.

key_findings.claim: The equal-training-budget appendix weakens the claim that interpretability is obtained without compromising performance.
key_findings.evidence: Table B1 compares B-cosified models with standard models further trained to the same effective 180 epochs. Ten of twelve converted architectures are lower than the further-trained standard counterpart, including ViT-Ti by 2.8 points, ViTc-Ti by 2.5, ViT-S by 1.2, and ViTc-S by 0.9; only ResNet-18 and DenseNet-121 are slightly higher. The main-table comparison to a frozen initial checkpoint therefore omits the opportunity cost of using the same fine-tuning budget on the original model.

key_findings.claim: The reported speedup is a narrow learning-curve statistic, not a matched measurement of end-to-end training cost.
key_findings.evidence: Speedup is computed as 90 divided by the fine-tuning epoch at which a converted model reaches the final accuracy of a scratch B-cos model. It is not measured in FLOPs, GPU-hours, wall time, energy, data passes including pretraining, or hyperparameter-search cost. Treating the pretrained checkpoint as a reusable sunk asset can be operationally reasonable, but the headline should be read as marginal epoch savings under that assumption.

key_findings.claim: Grid Pointing Game demonstrates class-specific spatial concentration on synthetic mosaics, not general interpretability or natural-scene causal faithfulness.
key_findings.evidence: The evaluation composes grids of independently sampled class images and measures how much positive attribution for a class falls in the tile containing that class. B-cosified W(x)x maps improve by roughly 32.7 to 71 points over conventional dynamic summaries and approach scratch B-cos models. The setup is useful for class specificity, but the mosaics are out of distribution and the score does not test human understanding, counterfactual necessity, insertion/deletion behavior, natural-object masks, or signed negative evidence.

key_findings.claim: Explanation quality is highly sensitive to architectural details that leave classification accuracy almost unchanged.
key_findings.evidence: In the single-run ResNet-18 design ablation, replacing uncentered batch normalization with centered normalization changes accuracy from 71.5% to 71.0% but localization from 86.8 to 28.8. Restoring conventional global-average-pooling order leaves accuracy at 71.5% while localization falls to 63.8. This 58-point and 23-point sensitivity makes automated equivalence and explanation-regression tests essential.

anchors.section: Appendix B and Table B4, architecture-design ablations

key_findings.claim: Weight normalization and schedule ablations show that the recommended unnormalized, immediate-change recipe is not uniformly optimal.
key_findings.evidence: Table B2 shows normalized B-cos weights improve several ViT variants substantially, including gains over the original checkpoint for ViT-S, ViT-B, ViTc-S, and ViTc-B, while hurting ViT-Ti. Tables B5 and B6 show strong sensitivity to B schedules and that bias decay can exceed immediate bias removal in localization. The conversion rule is therefore architecture-dependent despite its deliberately simple default.

key_findings.claim: The CLIP experiment is a useful proof of concept but covers only the older ResNet-50 visual encoder and a constrained re-training setup, not modern vision-language foundation models generally.
key_findings.evidence: The paper B-cosifies CLIP RN50, freezes the original text encoder, and fine-tunes or distills the image encoder for 90 epochs on ImageNet or CC3M with a SigLIP-style objective. It does not test ViT-based CLIP, OpenCLIP scale, SigLIP, modern self-supervised encoders, instruction-tuned multimodal models, or large dense-prediction backbones. The broad foundation-model framing exceeds this one visual-encoder family.

key_findings.claim: B-cosified CLIP remains usable across broad benchmark panels, but the original CLIP commonly retains stronger zero-shot performance.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 and Tables B7-B8 compare 38 zero-shot and 29 linear-probe datasets. The converted variants consistently beat Text2Concept on the paper's natural and specialized groupings and can be competitive on structured tasks, but original CLIP is frequently the best natural or specialized zero-shot baseline. The evidence supports retained zero-shot capability with trade-offs, not unchanged CLIP behavior.

key_findings.claim: FeatureCLIP's strongest high-power localization maps explain a newly constructed sharpened local readout, not the ordinary CLIP similarity score.
key_findings.evidence: The method removes the original query-key attention pooling, obtains per-location projected values, computes text cosine similarity at every location, raises the magnitude by a power p, and averages. Values p=1, 7, 19, and infinity are evaluated, with high p improving VOC energy pointing. Because p greater than one and max pooling alter the scalar whose gradient and dynamic map are computed, output completeness applies to that altered local objective; fidelity to the standard CLIP score is not established.

key_findings.claim: Energy Pointing Game on VOC measures positive-attribution localization inside boxes and cannot validate the paper's human-interpretability claim by itself.
key_findings.evidence: The CLIP localization score is the proportion of positive attribution energy inside ground-truth bounding boxes. It rewards spatial concentration but ignores negative evidence, explanation comprehensibility, semantic naming, causal intervention, and whether the same map helps a person make or contest a decision. The paper provides qualitative examples but no user study.

key_findings.claim: The attribution baseline panel is too narrow to establish current state-of-the-art explanation quality.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 4 compares W(x)x with Guided Backpropagation, raw gradients, DeepLIFT, input-times-gradient, Integrated Gradients, and GradCAM. The paper does not compare with then-available CLIP Surgery, Grounding Everything, or ClearCLIP, nor later stronger probing and ViT attribution methods. Many of those methods are post-hoc rather than inherently complete, but they are necessary quality and compute baselines.

key_findings.claim: The uncertainty record is internally inconsistent: the checklist says every experimental result uses three runs, while four appendix ablation tables explicitly report single runs.
key_findings.evidence: Table B2 states three-run averages, but the captions of Tables B3, B4, B5, and B6 describe random-initialized single-run results. key_findings.claim: The paper does not test whether B-cosification sharpens undesirable or brittle evidence along with desired class-specific evidence.
key_findings.evidence: Experiments cover in-distribution ImageNet accuracy, synthetic-grid localization, CLIP Benchmark transfer, and VOC box localization. They omit ImageNet-A/R/Sketch/ObjectNet, corruptions, adversarial perturbations, calibration, spurious-correlation sets, subgroup fairness, shortcut sensitivity, insertion/deletion, model-parameter randomization, and counterfactual interventions. A high localization proxy can coexist with reliance on a wrong but spatially concentrated cue.

Discussion and limitations

key_findings.claim: The paper's own limitations discussion is much narrower than the evidence warrants.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion emphasizes slower convergence of B-cos models and the absence of speedups for the largest convolutional ViTs. It does not foreground the proxy nature of GridPG and EPG, the absence of humans and causal tests, equal-budget accuracy losses, architecture fragility, narrow CLIP scope, statistical inconsistencies, outdated baselines, or distribution-shift and fairness gaps.

anchors.section: Discussion, limitations and conclusion

key_findings.claim: The absolute experimental cost is substantial even if converting an existing checkpoint is cheaper than training a B-cos counterpart from scratch.
key_findings.evidence: The checklist reports A100-SXM4-40GB and Quadro RTX 8000 hardware, typically four GPUs per run and eight A100s for ViTs, one to two days for standard and ImageNet-CLIP jobs, roughly 28 days for CC3M CLIP training, approximately 500 runs, and about 2.5 TB of storage. This supports a relative amortized-cost claim, not an unqualified low-cost claim.

key_findings.claim: The release is useful for rerunning training and loading checkpoints but falls short of a complete auditable artifact for the paper's main claims.
key_findings.evidence: The paper promises code, checkpoints, PyTorch implementation details, and Captum visualizations. The current repository supplies pinned dependencies, commands, model assets, and an Apache-2.0 code license, but its own conversion code has no tests or CI, no packaged seeds or result tables, and no evident end-to-end reproducer for Figure 6's EPG curves. The CLIP localization script also contains an unconditional CUDA path. These artifact observations were checked against the current attributable repository rather than inferred from the PDF alone.

key_findings.claim: The strongest retrospective value is the practical pretrained-to-B-cos conversion recipe and FeatureCLIP construction, while the underlying B-cos transform and localization metrics are inherited.
key_findings.evidence: The paper builds directly on B-cos Networks and their dynamic-linear W(x)x explanation and GridPG evaluation. Its distinct contribution is resolving input encoding, normalization, activations, biases, pooling, and transformer/CLIP compatibility well enough to initialize from conventional checkpoints, then demonstrating a prompt-conditioned local readout. This is substantial engineering novelty, but not a new definition or independently human-validated theory of interpretability.

method.core_idea: Rewrite a pretrained vision network as a B-cos-compatible dynamic-linear model at B=1, then fine-tune it after increasing B and removing affine biases so that its output admits a complete input-contribution summary W(x)x.
method.mechanism: The conversion expands centered RGB into six inverse-color channels with paired first-layer weights, retains ReLU as a gate, leaves pretrained weights unnormalized, replaces centered normalization and conventional pooling where required, removes biases, sets B=2 immediately, and fine-tunes for 90 epochs. CNN and ViT gates are folded into a per-input linear mapping. For CLIP RN50, the text encoder stays frozen while the image encoder is converted and trained on ImageNet or CC3M; FeatureCLIP exposes projected spatial values and aggregates text similarities with a cosine power p.
assumptions: The six-channel algebra matches the exact input normalization and first-layer convention used by the pretrained model.
Weight-normalization invariance is reliable mainly where each affected layer is followed by a normalization layer.
Activation, attention, and GELU gates can be treated as fixed for the evaluated input when forming W(x).
Deleting all intermediate biases is acceptable after fine-tuning and the remaining logit treatment is declared explicitly.
The chosen scalar output and any pooling or cosine-power transformation are the quantity the explanation is meant to reconstruct.
GridPG and EPG localization are informative proxies for the intended notion of interpretability.
An existing pretrained checkpoint is a reusable asset whose original training cost can be amortized rather than charged to conversion.
ImageNet and CC3M fine-tuning preserve enough of the original representation to support the tested transfer tasks.
Comparisons with published scratch B-cos numbers are sufficiently matched in architecture and preprocessing.
Positive attribution concentration captures the desired evidence even when signed negative contributions are not scored.

techniques.role: Replaces a linear projection with an input-dependent alignment-weighted projection controlled by exponent B.
Composes bias-free gated layers into the exact per-input linear summary y(x)=W(x)x.
Maps three centered color channels to six color-and-inverse channels for signed colored explanations.
Pairs positive and inverse first-layer weights so the six-channel response equals the original RGB response.
Retains pretrained ReLU behavior and incorporates its activation mask into the dynamic-linear summary.
Keeps pretrained weights unnormalized in the default recipe to reduce initialization shift.
Removes affine biases immediately to obtain complete input-only decompositions.
Raises B from the function-preserving value one to the target value two before fine-tuning.
Uses scale-only normalization so centering offsets do not break the bias-free decomposition.
Moves global averaging relative to the final projection to preserve interpretable spatial contributions.
Folds attention and GELU gates into a dynamic-linear explanation for transformer architectures.
Scores class-specific positive attribution inside the correct tile of a synthetic multi-image grid.
Fine-tunes the converted CLIP RN50 image encoder against a frozen text encoder on ImageNet or CC3M.
Exposes each projected spatial value from CLIP attention pooling instead of producing one query-key-pooled vector.
Sharpens per-location text-image cosine scores with powers from one through max-like infinity.
Measures the fraction of positive attribution energy inside Pascal VOC bounding boxes.
Evaluates zero-shot and frozen-feature linear-probe transfer over the CLIP Benchmark dataset panels.

limitations: Exact W(x)x output reconstruction is not equivalent to human interpretability, semantic correctness, causal faithfulness, robustness, or minimality.
GridPG uses artificial image mosaics and EPG uses positive energy inside bounding boxes; neither is a human or interventional validation.
The main performance comparison favors the weaker scratch B-cos endpoint rather than the same-budget further-trained standard model.
The speedup metric counts epochs to a reference accuracy, not FLOPs, GPU-hours, wall time, energy, data, or hyperparameter search.
Pretraining cost is treated as sunk; this is valid only when the checkpoint is already available and sufficiently reusable.
B-cosification loses material accuracy for some strong checkpoints, especially supervised ResNet-50 v2 and small ViTs.
Architecture choices such as batch-normalization centering and pooling order can destroy localization while leaving accuracy nearly unchanged.
The default unnormalized, B=2, immediate-zero-bias recipe is not optimal for every architecture in the paper's own ablations.
CLIP evidence is limited to the old RN50 image encoder with a frozen original text encoder and ImageNet or CC3M fine-tuning.
FeatureCLIP with p greater than one explains an altered sharpened spatial objective, not standard CLIP similarity.
The attribution panel omits strong contemporaneous CLIP-localization methods and later stronger ViT attribution methods.
The study contains no human evaluation despite repeatedly describing explanations as highly human interpretable.
No insertion, deletion, counterfactual, parameter-randomization, or explanation-invariance test evaluates causal or behavioral faithfulness.
No distribution-shift, corruption, adversarial, shortcut, subgroup-fairness, or calibration evaluation is reported.
Positive-only localization scores discard negative evidence from the signed dynamic-linear decomposition.
Several appendix ablations are single runs despite the checklist's statement that every experimental result uses three runs.
The meaning of plus/minus uncertainty in main tables is not defined and most comparisons lack formal statistical testing.
Published baseline results are not all rerun under matched data, compute, schedules, seeds, and implementation.
The qualitative galleries have no blinded sampling protocol, user task, or quantified stability across seeds, prompts, and transforms.
The current artifact lacks first-party tests, first-party CI, packaged result logs, and an evident quantitative FeatureCLIP EPG reproducer.
failure_modes: A converted module without the assumed following normalization can violate the claimed invariance to pretrained weight norms.
Leaving a hidden bias, centered normalization offset, or incompatible residual path can make the displayed input contributions incomplete.
Using conventional global-pooling order can retain accuracy while sharply degrading spatial explanations.
A high B can sharpen any aligned cue, including background, texture, watermark, demographic, or adversarial correlations.
A high GridPG score on out-of-distribution mosaics can fail to transfer to cluttered natural multi-object scenes.
Positive-energy metrics can hide decisive negative evidence or sign cancellation.
Smoothing, percentile clipping, alpha blending, color mapping, and class-logit choice can make identical contributions look qualitatively different.
FeatureCLIP power tuning can optimize box localization while drifting far from the ordinary CLIP score being presented as explained.
Fine-tuning on ImageNet can erode zero-shot language alignment even when in-domain classification improves.
Fine-tuning on CC3M for 28 days can erase the practical cost advantage for teams that only need occasional explanations.
The optimal bias and weight-normalization schedule can vary by architecture, so a universal recipe can silently sacrifice accuracy or localization.
Single-run ablations can overstate fragile ordering among schedules or initialization sources.
A map can reconstruct a score exactly yet remain spatially diffuse, unstable, uninterpretable to people, or causally misleading under intervention.
No-tests conversion code can regress architectural equivalence while checkpoints still produce plausible accuracy.
An unconditional CUDA call in the CLIP localization path can break CPU or nonstandard-device reproduction.
Downstream developers can overtrust persuasive inherent maps because the paper's broader-impact discussion emphasizes benefits without calibrating explanation uncertainty.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A simple, low-cost method for transforming pretrained conventional CNNs, vision transformers, and CLIP into inherently interpretable B-cos models that outperform scratch B-cos training, often recover original accuracy, and retain broad zero-shot capability.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The six-channel equivalence, module-by-module conversion, ImageNet panel, GridPG gains, CLIP Benchmark, and FeatureCLIP localization demonstrate a genuine and useful pretrained-to-B-cos pipeline across several 2024-era architectures. The paper reports a 2.5-point average gain over scratch B-cos and 5.2x average epoch speedup, with strong localization gains.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Novelty was moderately high at publication because the paper made B-cos models practically reachable from standard checkpoints and extended the idea to a vision-language model. The core B-cos operator, exact dynamic-linear explanation, and GridPG metric were inherited; the new work is the conversion recipe and FeatureCLIP readout. The 2026 closest successor ALOE now substantially supersedes vanilla B-cosification for supervised ViTs, DINOv3, and SigLIP2 through one-time label-free feature alignment, broader transfer and dense-task evaluation, and human-preference and deletion tests. DAVE further shows that exact inherent B-cos maps need not optimize localization metrics. The reviewed work remains an important engineering precursor and baseline, but its general foundation-model and human-interpretability claims are no longer frontier evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: B-cos Alignment for Inherently Interpretable CNNs and Vision Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Primary architectural foundation whose B-cos operator, dynamic-linear explanations, and evaluation are reused.
competitive_landscape.difference: B-cos Alignment trains interpretable CNNs and ViTs directly around alignment pressure; B-cosification contributes a checkpoint-conversion and fine-tuning recipe intended to avoid full scratch training.

competitive_landscape.title: B-cos LM: Efficiently Transforming Pre-trained Language Models for Improved Explainability
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct cross-modal successor applying B-cosification principles to pretrained language models.
competitive_landscape.difference: B-cos LM extends conversion beyond vision and adds automatic and human evaluation; it also reports that stronger alignment can amplify spurious correlations, a risk not tested in the reviewed vision paper.

competitive_landscape.title: DAVE: Distribution-aware Attribution via ViT Gradient Decomposition
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current mathematically structured post-hoc ViT attribution competitor evaluated against B-cos maps.
competitive_landscape.difference: DAVE decomposes gradients without retraining the backbone and can improve GridPG or EPG even on B-cos models; this separates exact inherent output decomposition from the attribution map that best satisfies localization metrics.

competitive_landscape.title: How to Probe: Simple Yet Effective Techniques for Improving Post-hoc Explanations
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct evidence that the classifier head and its training objective strongly control explanation quality.
competitive_landscape.difference: How to Probe changes less than ten percent of parameters and improves class specificity across pretrained models and attribution methods; it is a cheaper post-hoc-quality baseline and makes matched head training important when judging B-cosification.

competitive_landscape.title: Hidden in Plain Sight -- Class Competition Focuses Attribution Maps
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-hoc class-contrastive competitor targeting the same GridPG class-specific localization failure.
competitive_landscape.difference: Its VAR aggregation focuses existing attribution maps without converting the backbone, showing that class competition alone can produce large localization gains and should be separated from inherent-completeness claims.

competitive_landscape.title: A Closer Look at the Explainability of Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporaneous training-free CLIP localization competitor, commonly called CLIP Surgery.
competitive_landscape.difference: CLIP Surgery modifies inference-time feature and attention interactions to improve open-vocabulary localization without 90-epoch image-encoder fine-tuning; it lacks B-cos output completeness but is a necessary quality, cost, and preservation baseline absent from the paper.

competitive_landscape.title: Grounding Everything: Emerging Localization Properties in Vision-Language Transformers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporaneous vision-language localization method using self-self attention and feature grouping.
competitive_landscape.difference: GEM exposes training-free or lightweight emerging localization across multiple VLM backbones and segmentation datasets; B-cosified CLIP instead retrains RN50 for inherent score decomposition and tests VOC box energy.

competitive_landscape.title: ClearCLIP: Decomposing CLIP Representations for Dense Vision-Language Inference
competitive_landscape.relationship: Contemporaneous training-free dense CLIP representation competitor submitted before B-cosification.
competitive_landscape.difference: ClearCLIP removes selected final residual and feed-forward paths and uses self-self attention to improve dense inference across eight datasets; it preserves the pretrained model differently and does not claim a complete B-cos decomposition.

competitive_landscape.title: LeGrad: An Explainability Method for Vision Transformers via Feature Formation Sensitivity
competitive_landscape.relationship: Strong post-hoc ViT and vision-language attribution competitor available before the paper's final revision.
competitive_landscape.difference: LeGrad aggregates gradients over attention layers to explain feature formation without converting or fine-tuning the model; it competes on map quality and preservation but not on exact inherent decomposition.

competitive_landscape.title: This Looks Like That: Deep Learning for Interpretable Image Recognition
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational interpretable-by-design visual classifier offering case-based rather than pixel-attribution explanations.
competitive_landscape.difference: ProtoPNet traces a decision through learned human-inspectable prototypes and training examples, providing a different global and local explanation object; B-cosification preserves broader backbone families but exposes signed pixel contributions without semantic names.

competitive_landscape.title: ProtoPFormer: Concentrating on Prototypical Parts in Vision Transformers for Interpretable Image Recognition
competitive_landscape.relationship: Interpretable-by-design ViT competitor based on global and local prototypes.
competitive_landscape.difference: ProtoPFormer explicitly supervises prototype focus and supplies case-based parts, whereas B-cosification retains a pretrained transformer's topology and explains scores through dense input contributions.

competitive_landscape.title: FaCT: Faithful Concept Traces for Explaining Neural Network Decisions
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current inherently interpretable vision model connecting pixels, learned concepts, and logits.
competitive_landscape.difference: FaCT supplies semantically assessable concept traces, a concept-consistency metric, and a user study; B-cosification offers exact pixel-to-score maps over more pretrained architectures but no concept semantics or human validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Concept Bottleneck Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational interpretable-by-design paradigm supporting named concepts and interventions.
competitive_landscape.difference: Concept bottlenecks expose and permit intervention on a supervised semantic layer, while B-cosification avoids concept annotation and retrofits dense pixel contributions but cannot directly name or edit its evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: Concept Bottleneck Models Without Predefined Concepts
competitive_landscape.relationship: Post-hoc conversion competitor that discovers concepts without a predefined concept list.
competitive_landscape.difference: This approach converts a pretrained black box into a concept bottleneck through unsupervised concept discovery, targeting semantic global explanations; B-cosification targets exact signed pixel-level decomposition and tests localization instead.

competitive_landscape.title: Concept Bottleneck Model with Zero Performance Loss
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct retrofit competitor emphasizing exact prediction preservation.
competitive_landscape.difference: The method inserts an invertible latent-to-concept mapping into an off-the-shelf black box and exactly preserves predictions, whereas B-cosification changes the model through 90-epoch fine-tuning and can lose accuracy while gaining pixel attribution.

competitive_landscape.title: Capability != Interpretability: Human Interpretability of Vision Foundation Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current human-centered measurement work challenging capability or localization as an interpretability proxy.
competitive_landscape.difference: It uses localizability and nameability protocols with 377 participants and more than 13,000 valid responses, finding interpretability distinct from task capability; B-cosification infers human interpretability from attribution appearance and localization scores without participants.

competitive_landscape.title: CFM: Language-aligned Concept Foundation Model for Vision
competitive_landscape.relationship: Current concept-based foundation-model alternative with spatially grounded language-aligned features.
competitive_landscape.difference: CFM exposes reusable named concepts across classification, segmentation, and captioning, while B-cosified CLIP exposes prompt-conditioned pixel evidence from one RN50 conversion without a reusable concept vocabulary.

open_questions: Can a converter compile arbitrary PyTorch or JAX module graphs into B-cos form and prove numerical B=1 equivalence with property tests?
Which normalization, residual, pooling, activation, and attention patterns admit exact bias-free dynamic-linear summaries without architecture-specific surgery?
Can an exact explanation contract specify the scalar, detach convention, aggregation, sign, residual term, and rendering so every map is numerically reconstructible?
How does B trade off task accuracy, localization, causal faithfulness, stability, and reliance on spurious correlations across architectures?
Do deletion, insertion, counterfactual retraining, causal mediation, and parameter-randomization tests agree with GridPG and EPG rankings?
Do B-cos maps improve human nameability, localizability, error detection, model comparison, and calibrated decision-making in preregistered user studies?
How should FeatureCLIP sparsify spatial evidence while preserving the original CLIP similarity exactly rather than replacing it with a powered local readout?
Can one expose both the ordinary CLIP score decomposition and an explicitly separate localization-optimized readout in the same interface?
How well does label-free feature alignment such as ALOE generalize to current SigLIP, DINO, video, multimodal, and dense-prediction foundation models?
Can B-cos pixel evidence be composed with named concepts or prototypes to provide exact pixel-to-concept-to-logit traces?
What happens under ImageNet-A/R/Sketch/ObjectNet, corruptions, adversarial attacks, background swaps, watermark shortcuts, and subgroup shifts?
Can explanation uncertainty be calibrated from seeds, augmentations, prompts, checkpoints, and local perturbations?
What is the total lifecycle cost under matched data, FLOPs, GPU-hours, energy, tuning, storage, and amortized checkpoint reuse?
Can automated architecture-sensitivity analysis identify and repair centered normalization or pooling changes before localization silently collapses?
When can a post-hoc decomposition such as DAVE outperform an exact inherent map, and what does that reveal about metric validity?
How much of the reported gain persists when all post-hoc, concept, prototype, and conversion baselines receive matched heads, tuning data, and compute?
Can model editing guided by B-cos evidence remove a shortcut while preserving unrelated behavior, thereby turning explanations into validated interventions?
reusable_insights: An explanation method should publish an explicit explanation contract: target scalar, exact reconstruction equation, detach rules, aggregation, sign handling, and rendering transform.
Initialization equivalence and post-fine-tuning interpretability are separate claims and should be tested independently.
Every architecture converter needs numerical function-equivalence tests at the neutral setting and explanation-reconstruction tests after conversion.
Interpretability evaluation should combine completeness, causal intervention, natural localization, human task utility, stability, robustness, and semantic quality rather than one pointing score.
Grid-based class specificity, bounding-box energy, and human comprehension should be displayed as distinct axes in the atlas.
Positive-only attribution metrics should be paired with signed evidence accounting and reconstruction residuals.
Comparisons should report both change from the starting checkpoint and change from the same-budget further-trained checkpoint.
Efficiency claims should separate marginal conversion cost, amortized pretraining cost, and total lifecycle compute.
An epoch-to-reference speedup should never be presented as a hardware-independent compute speedup without FLOP or GPU-hour measurements.
Head choice, normalization centering, pooling order, logit bias, and visualization postprocessing belong in the experimental specification because they can dominate explanation scores.
Localization-optimized readouts must be labeled as new objectives when they differ from the model score users believe is being explained.
Human-interpretable should be reserved for measured human outcomes, while algebraically complete, localized, sparse, and visually sharp describe separate observable properties.
Current competitor panels should distinguish post-hoc quality, inherent completeness, semantic concepts, prediction preservation, and compute instead of collapsing them into one ranking.
A reproducible artifact should include one-command metric reproduction, pinned environments, released seeds and logs, CPU/device portability, first-party tests, and CI.
Explanation regression tests should fail when a code change preserves accuracy but materially changes reconstruction or localization.
A useful next benchmark would pair B-cosification, ALOE, DAVE, CLIP Surgery, ClearCLIP, prototype models, and concept traces under matched teachers, heads, data, and human evaluation.
reviewer_notes: Primary full-text review of all 31 pages in the hash-pinned cached arXiv v2 PDF, whose current arXiv revision is dated 2025-01-24 and whose paper appeared at NeurIPS 2024. I read the ten-page main paper, all three reference pages, Appendices A-C, and every checklist page. I visually audited all pages through contact sheets and inspected every substantive plot, table, diagram, and qualitative panel at original resolution. The audit covered all nine numbered figures (Figures 1-6 and A1-A3) and all twelve tables (Tables 1-4 and B1-B8), including their captions, uncertainty notation, and single-run disclosures. Current primary-source competitor checking covered original B-cos work, B-cos LM, DAVE, How to Probe, class-contrastive VAR, CLIP Surgery, GEM, ClearCLIP, LeGrad, prototype networks, concept bottlenecks, FaCT, CFM, and human interpretability measurement. I also checked the closest current successor, ALOE (CVPR 2026), from its official project paper and current attributable repository: its one-time label-free global-and-token feature alignment over supervised ViTs, DINOv3, and SigLIP2 substantially improves on vanilla B-cosification and evaluates broader transfer, dense prediction, pixel deletion, and human preference. Because the atlas validator currently accepts only its fixed primary-archive host set and neither the ALOE institutional paper URL nor official project host is in that set, ALOE is documented here and in the novelty audit rather than inserted with a non-resolving proceedings URL. I inspected the reviewed paper's current attributable artifact at commit 289e9920066d8abd5ed1f6ab07acd49d2642c810 (latest commit 2025-10-13): 192 files, 16 commits, Python 3.12.2 and pinned PyTorch/Captum dependencies, commands, Apache-2.0 code license, ImageNet-derived model-use warning, and released supervised and CLIP checkpoints. Its first-party sources compile, but it has no first-party tests or CI; tests and workflows belong to vendored CLIP components, quantitative FeatureCLIP EPG reproduction is not evident, and text_localisation.py contains an unconditional CUDA token path. Code and CLIP checkpoints first appeared after the final arXiv revision. Numeric values above are transcribed from the PDF's tables, captions, or text; the distinction between exact decomposition and semantic or causal interpretability, and between powered FeatureCLIP readouts and ordinary CLIP similarity, is reviewer analysis.
